item.title: Andy Statman Trio at Barbès
item.description: Andy Statman Trio at BarbèsFeb. 4. 8PM. $22.50 In a music career that goes back to the 1970s, Andy Statman has pursued two distinct paths. He made a name for himself on the New York bluegrass scene as a mandolin virtuoso, but he also became a key player in the revival of Jewish klezmer music as a clarinetist. Eventually, Statman combined his love of jazz with the spiritual melodies of the Hassidic mystics of centuries gone by. Andy Statman and his trio play Feb. 4 at Barbès in Brooklyn

item.title: Sangjaru at Joe's Pub
item.description: Sangjaru at Joe's PubFeb. 4. 7PM. $36 The sounds of traditional Korean music meet the instruments and rhythms of Western rock, folk, and jazz in the band Sangjaru. Based in Seoul, South Korea, the band uses instruments we all know, like the guitar, with less familiar things, like the janggu (hourglass drum) or the zither known as the kayageum, which is normally plucked but which Sangjaru often plays with a cello bow. Sangjaru plays on Feb. 4 at Joe’s Pub.

item.title: Sprints at Bowery Ballroom
item.description: Sprints at Bowery BallroomFeb. 5. 7:30PM. $34.85 The rock band Sprints comes from Dublin, where they made a name for themselves as a take-no-prisoners live band while releasing a couple of well-received EPs. Their debut LP came out in 2023 and was followed by a second record this past fall, both full of walls of sound inspired by post-punk and grunge. item.title: The George Gee Swing Orchestra Meets the Arturo O'Farrill Afro-Latin Octet at Flushing Town Hall
item.description: The George Gee Swing Orchestra Meets the Arturo O'Farrill Afro-Latin Octet at Flushing Town HallFeb. 7. 7PM Dance Lessons. 8PM Performance. $25+up The George Gee Swing Orchestra started way back in 1980, bringing old-time big band music to New York listeners – and more important, to dancers. The band has played for years at the Manhattan club Swing 46, where people who remember the Charleston and the lindy hop can strut their stuff. Now they’re bringing their swinging sound to Flushing Town Hall
